text:
Aisha: Heads up — after yesterday's small-preparse refactor I'm seeing a consistent +10-15ms on p95 for short requests (<=64 tokens). Digging in now :eyes:
Mike: Which service/route? can you paste p95/p99 before/after?
Aisha: api-proxy -> host-preproc path. Before: p95=28ms p99=55ms. After: p95=40ms p99=70ms. Baseline traffic synthetic 500rps small prompts.
Sam: Any KV cache differences? more misses?
Aisha: KV hitrate steady (~98%). Not KV. Kernel selection also unchanged (same model bin chosen). Suspect host-side tokenize+framing and grpc small-write coalesce.
Mike: Could be smallwrite/writev batching regression. We changed preparse inline to avoid copy; might be increasing syscall count per chunk. Can you grab a short strace/procstat or a pprof of rpc handler?
Aisha: Pprof of CPU on host-preproc attached (cut):
```
(pprof) top10
  23.4%  host_preproc
   8.9%  host_preproc.tokenize
   6.7%  host_preproc.stream_frame
   3.5%  net.writev
   2.1%  proto.serialize
```
```
strace snippet: repeated writev of ~128b frames, ~3-4 syscalls per response rather than 1.
```
writev(fd, iov, 2) = 128
writev(fd, iov, 1) = 64
```
Mike: That matches. The inline preparse likely created separate buffers instead of coalescing into single iov. ingress-bot: deploy/2112 succeeded (preparse-refactor).
Sam: I'll add a microbench that simulates small prompt path and compares writev count. Also toggling smallwrite coalesce in proxy config could be quick test.
Leo: Quick experiment — I pushed a proxy flag to force coalesce (proxy.coalesce_small_writes=true) on a canary pool. Results after 1h: p95 dropped from 40ms -> 30ms, p99 from 70ms -> 50ms. writev syscall count per request reduced ~3x. :thumbsup:
Aisha: Nice. So the refactor reduced copying but harmed IOV composition. Kernel selection and batching heuristics unaffected. The extra host-tokenize fragmentation dominates.
Mike: Proposed fix: change preparse to populate a single contiguous buffer for the final framed payload (one writev per response) OR re-enable coalesce at host-proxy layer. Which is lower risk?
Sam: Low-risk: keep refactor but update host-proxy to coalesce writes (fast config). Long-term: update preparse to use a single append buffer and avoid small slices. I'll open PRs.
Aisha: Filing perf PR with bench results + pprof attached. Also instrument KV cache hooks to confirm no regressions.
Mike: One more note — batcher heuristic might be skewed by extra latency; if host preparse adds 10ms it can change batching windows. We should run a microbench for batching lag vs this host overhead. Add to TODO.
Leo: I'll schedule a quick canary to roll proxy coalesce to all canary hosts tonight.
Aisha: Thanks. Summary: regression traced to increased small writev ops from preparse refactor; workaround via proxy coalesce improves tail. Next: PR to preparse single-buffer, batching microbench, KV instrumentation. :hammer:
